care_continuity: National isolation/CTE stock: 1091; provincial clinical scopes and missing reports remain explicit.
Ituri: 499 patients; printed occupancy 48.0; current source scope retained.
Nord-Kivu: 468 patients; printed occupancy 80.7; current source scope retained.
Tshopo: 9 patients; printed occupancy 25.0; current source scope retained.
Bas-Uele: 86 patients; printed occupancy None; current source scope retained.
challenges: Contact follow-up is 28615/33736 (84.8%), below 95%; Nord-Kivu 83.0%, Tshopo 80.0%. Key messages identify Lita 32.5%, Kalunguta 54.7% and Nia-Nia 59.6% as critical.

481 suspects validated, 469 investigated (97.5%), 255 transferred (54.4% of investigated). The source says 12 suspects remain uninvestigated, its zone list also totals 12 but includes a negative value of -5 at Nia-Nia; preserve the inconsistency. None of the 26 Bas-Uele suspects and only one of 12 Tshopo suspects was transferred.

Butuhe PoC remains closed after the 26 September security incident; Nord-Kivu lacks IPC supplies, PPE and a dedicated ambulance. Ituri reports two of three suspects refusing transfer and Avakubi closed for insecurity. Sud-Kivu reporting is 55.6%, without isolation facilities at PoE. Haut-Uele has two of ten PoC not reporting; Bas-Uele lacks training, water, mobility and digitalisation.

Ituri: 17/46 rings unopened, three of 50 households not decontaminated, 23 EDS failures, 20/70 bodies not swabbed and 13 postponed EDS. Nord-Kivu: 22/51 rings unopened, 22/33 households not decontaminated, no kits for 11 households and 45 postponed EDS. Tshopo has four unswabbed bodies and critical IPC stock. Bas-Uele has 16/20 priority facilities without triage.

Ituri lacks blood and capacity at Kilo, Lolwa, Mandima and Biakato; 18 Mandima patients received no food. Nord-Kivu has 173/192 suspect beds occupied (90.1%), 137/468 patients outside CTE/CT and 79% data completeness. Tshopo reports five confirmed patients still in the community. Bas-Uele lacks a standard CTE, nutrition, ambulance and timely psychosocial support.

Ituri reports 1311 people vaccinated and 28 adverse events (two serious); target population needs redefining. Bas-Uele cold-chain units are not running; vaccination has not begun at Ango (0/2247) or Bili (0/1067). Nord-Kivu data did not arrive; Haut-Uele questions PPL-only targeting. These observations establish no vaccine efficacy against BDBV.

Katwa hospital evaluation finds no simplified continuity plan or adequate triage, shortages of PPE and blood products, and no ambulance or contingency plan for staff absenteeism; 18/178 providers absent and three exposed or quarantined. Komanda triage is poorly functional; maternity and child-care attendance is falling in Tshopo.

Ituri psychosocial support covers 15/28 affected zones; 18/37 latest confirmed cases not supported, notably Mandima. Nord-Kivu has low coverage and ten affected zones without creches or reinsertion resources. Bas-Uele support remains delayed.
Ituri community engagement reporting is only 11/28 zones (39.3%). Nord-Kivu received 440/650 expected alerts (67.7%) and resolved two of two incidents.

Insecurity persists in 17 health areas of Mambasa and Mandima; resistance is reported in Rungu and threats to response teams in Bafwasende. Bas-Uele diesel stock is exhausted while Buta CTE construction continues.
